title: Life of God ambiguous: in Himself and in us; natural and spiritual
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): but ye formal consists in ye position belonging toward ye most supereminent mode belonging toward spiritual life by means belonging toward that same which God stands as active in Himself plus outside Himself. namely God's highest perfection; — the material in this attribute also stands as ye same as in ye others. but belonging toward that same we chiefly treat here — namely that same by means belonging toward that same which God lives in Himself, that same which stands as God Himself, plus stands as conceived by means belonging toward us as ye second moment belonging toward ye divine nature — not belonging toward this. plus in 2 Corinthians 4:11 ye life belonging toward Jesus — and this stands as that same life that same which to ye Ephesians stands as called ye life belonging toward God. plus stands as nothing other than perfect motion out from ye action belonging toward ye Holy Spirit, who stands as as it were ye soul belonging toward ye regenerate man: — spiritual stands as that same life that same which we have through ye second generation in Christ. of this it stands as said in Acts 17:28, In Him we live plus move plus are. plus stands as nothing other than ye function belonging toward ye rational soul in moving, sensing, plus reasoning; — natural stands as that same life that same which we have through ye first generation in Adam. he says, stands as twofold, natural plus spiritual — the life belonging toward man. Of that same which also Irenaeus, Against Heresies book V chapter 13: saying ye Gentiles stand as alienated out from ye life belonging toward God — of ye latter Paul speaks in Ephesians 4:18. or that same by means belonging toward that same which He lives in us — either that same by means belonging toward that same which He Himself lives in Himself. The life belonging toward God stands as said ambiguously:
pass_b_english: The life of God is said ambiguously: either that by which He Himself lives in Himself, or that by which He lives in us. Of the latter Paul speaks in Ephesians 4:18, saying the Gentiles are alienated from the life of God. Of which also Irenaeus, Against Heresies book V chapter 13: The life of man, he says, is twofold, natural and spiritual.

Natural is that life which we have through the first generation in Adam, and is nothing other than the function of the rational soul in moving, sensing, and reasoning; of this it is said in Acts 17:28, In Him we live and move and are. Spiritual is that life which we have through the second generation in Christ, and is nothing other than perfect motion from the action of the Holy Spirit, who is as it were the soul of the regenerate man: and this is that life which to the Ephesians is called the life of God, and in 2 Corinthians 4:11 the life of Jesus.

Not of this, but of that we chiefly treat here — namely that by which God lives in Himself, which is God Himself, and is conceived by us as the second moment of the divine nature. The material in this attribute also is the same as in the others, namely God's highest perfection; but the formal consists in the position of the most supereminent mode of spiritual life by which God is active in Himself and outside Himself.
source_text: Vita Dei ambigue dicitur, vel qua ipse vivit in se, vel qua vivit in nobis. De hac Paulus loquitur Ephes. IV.18, dicens gentes alienatas esse a vita Dei. De qua etiam Irenaeus lib. V. adversus haereses cap. XIII: Vita, inquit, hominis duplex est, naturalis et spiritualis. Naturalis est vita illa quam habemus per primam generationem in Adamo, nihilque aliud est quam functio animae rationalis in movendo, sentiendo, ratiocinando; de hac dicitur Act. XVII.28: Per ipsum vivimus, movemur et sumus. Vita spiritualis est illa quam habemus per secundam generationem in Christo, nihilque aliud est quam motus perfectus ab actione Spiritus sancti, qui hominis regenerati tanquam anima est: atque haec est illa vita quae ad Ephesios dicitur vita Dei, et II Cor. IV.11 vita Jesu. Non de hac, sed de illa hic potissimum agimus, qua videlicet Deus vivit in se, quae Deus ipse est, et a nobis concipitur tanquam secundum naturae divinae momentum. Materiale quidem etiam in hoc attributo idem est quod in aliis, summa nempe Dei perfectio; formale vero est in positione modi spiritualis vitae supereminentissimi, quo Deus in se et extra se actuosus est.
